etna.options.title: Etna Shaders
etna.options.page.general.desc: Start here. Quality sets how much work Etna does, Look sets the colours and mood; the other pages fine-tune them. Every change shows right away. In game, F7 turns Etna on and off.
etna.options.page.lighting.desc: Sunlight, moonlight, shadows, and the faint light in caves.
etna.options.page.effects.desc: Anti-aliasing, ambient occlusion, glow and sharpening.
etna.options.page.colors.desc: The final colour grade. Moving any of these switches Look to Custom.
etna.options.enabled.desc: Turns Etna on or off. F7 does the same in game.
etna.options.quality.desc: Low: no shadows or anti-aliasing, the fastest. Medium: shadows close by. High: the recommended balance. Ultra: sharp shadows far away.
etna.options.profile.desc: Natural keeps Minecraft's own colours under real light. Soft is gentler and hazier, Vivid more saturated, Cinematic warmer with more contrast and glow.
etna.options.visibility.desc: How well you see in the dark, without making bright places brighter: caves get more of their faint light (with Cave Light on), sun and moon shadows get lighter, your eyes open up further in dark places (with Eye Adaptation on) and the darkest tones are lifted. Bright skies, snow and sunlit ground stay as they are. 0% (Off) is Etna 0.7.0's darkness. It stays where you put it when you change the Look.
etna.options.renderScale.desc: How many pixels the world is drawn at, as a share of the screen's width and height. Below 100% Etna draws the world smaller and its anti-aliasing builds the full picture back up over a few frames, the way DLSS and FSR do: much faster, a little softer, mostly in motion. 75% draws about half the pixels. The hand, the HUD and menus stay sharp. Needs anti-aliasing, which every Quality but Low has.
etna.options.resolution.desc: Half draws a quarter of the pixels and lets macOS scale the picture up: much faster, but blurry. Applies after restarting the game, and only when Etna is on as the game starts.
etna.options.shadows.desc: Real shadows cast by the sun and the moon.
etna.options.shadowResolution.desc: Detail of the shadow map: higher is sharper and slower.
etna.options.shadowDistance.desc: How far from you shadows are drawn. Further spreads the same detail over a bigger area.
etna.options.shadowSoftness.desc: How soft the edges of shadows are.
etna.options.shadowDarkness.desc: How dark the shade is next to sunlight.
etna.options.lightRays.desc: Shafts of sunlight through the air and the mist, golden when the sun is low and strongest under trees. Needs Shadows.
etna.options.antiAliasing.desc: Temporal anti-aliasing: smooth edges that stay still instead of crawling and flickering. Ambient Occlusion needs it; Sky Glow, Atmosphere and Mist need it or Shadows.
etna.options.ambientOcclusion.desc: Soft shade in corners, in cracks and under things.
etna.options.bloom.desc: A soft glow around the brightest things only: the sun, clouds, snow, flames and glowing blocks.
etna.options.haze.desc: Far terrain slowly takes the colour of the air.
etna.options.waterReflections.desc: Reflections on water: the sky, sun glints, and with Shadows or Anti-Aliasing on (and Improved Transparency off) the shore, trees and hills around it.
etna.options.eyeAdaptation.desc: Your eyes adjust to the light where you stand, over a few seconds: caves and nights read a little brighter, a sunny noon a little calmer, and at night, out under the sky, the darkest colours fade towards a cool moonlit grey. Off keeps the exposure fixed.
etna.options.contrast.desc: Deeper darks and brighter lights, without clipping either.
etna.options.vibrance.desc: Boosts dull colours more than vivid ones.
etna.options.warmth.desc: White balance: cooler and bluer, or warmer and more golden.
etna.options.vignette.desc: Darker corners of the screen, where they are dark: a bright sky or snow in a corner stays as it is.
etna.options.page.surfaces.desc: How blocks catch the light: the bumps in their textures, shine, leaves lit from behind, torchlight, blocks that glow, materials, puddles, sparkles and glowing flowers.
etna.options.page.sky.desc: The sky's colours, the glow around the sun and the air between you and the distance.
etna.options.surfaceDetail.desc: Gives block textures real bumps that catch the sun and throw tiny shadows, worked out from the textures themselves, so it works with any resource pack.
etna.options.shine.desc: Sun glints on smooth blocks, and wet, shiny ground when it rains.
etna.options.leafGlow.desc: Leaves and grass glow when the sun shines through them from behind.
etna.options.torchWarmth.desc: Warm orange light from torches, lanterns and lava, fading softly with distance.
etna.options.sunPathTilt.desc: How far the path of the sun and the moon leans to the south. Tilted, the noon sun stands to one side, south walls catch the light and shadows fall to the north. At 0 (Off) the sun keeps vanilla's path, straight overhead.
etna.options.skyGlow.desc: The warm glow the haze makes around the sun, strongest at sunrise and sunset.
etna.options.atmosphere.desc: Distant land fades into blue air, and towards the sun into a warm haze.
etna.options.cloudShadows.desc: Clouds drifting over the sun cast soft shadows that sweep across the land. Off when clouds are off in Video Settings.
etna.options.mist.desc: Low mist in the valleys at dawn and dusk, a soft haze at night and in the rain, and a faint murk deep in caves. Lit by the sun where it reaches.
etna.options.page.water.desc: How water looks from above and below: how far you see under water, its colour, and the light dancing on the seabed.
etna.options.caveLight.desc: Caves and dark rooms are never pitch black: a faint, cool light shows their shape.
etna.options.emission.desc: Lava, glowstone, sea lanterns and lanterns glow in the dark, brightly enough to bloom, and by day their glowing parts stay lit on the shaded sides too. Needs Smooth Lighting.
etna.options.underwaterVisibility.desc: How far you can see under water. Things far away fade into the water's colour, reds first.
etna.options.waterClarity.desc: How deep sunlight reaches when you are under water, and how clear shallow water looks from above (with Shadows on).
etna.options.caustics.desc: Rippling light the waves focus onto the ground, while you swim under water.
etna.options.underwaterRays.desc: Beams of sunlight through the water, and shade under overhangs. Needs Shadows.
etna.options.profiling.desc: Summary writes a line to latest.log every few seconds while you play: frame rate, frame time and where it goes, on the CPU and on the GPU (timed on one frame in eight, so the frame rate stays the normal one). Off writes nothing.
etna.options.benchmark.desc: Takes about 145 seconds, in a world: Etna tries its settings one at a time, writes what each one costs to latest.log, then puts everything back as it was. Stand still and don't move the mouse: a step disturbed by a camera move or a stutter is measured again, which can add up to about 20 seconds. Turn any frame-rate limiter mod and VSync off first.
etna.benchmark.start: Etna benchmark: stand still and don't move the mouse for about %s s; turn the frame-rate limiter mod off first.
etna.benchmark.done: Etna benchmark finished: the results are in latest.log.
etna.benchmark.unsteady: Etna benchmark finished, but the scene changed during the run: the results in latest.log are rough. Run it again, standing still, once the chunks around have loaded.
etna.benchmark.unavailable: Etna benchmark can't run: the performance log stopped after an error earlier in this session (see latest.log). Restart the game to try again.
etna.benchmark.stopped: Etna benchmark stopped: %s. Every setting is back as it was.
etna.benchmark.stopped.menu: a menu or loading screen opened
etna.benchmark.stopped.key: Etna was switched with its key
etna.options.page.mood.desc: A colour mood laid over the Look, made to suit the style of your resource pack, or a purely magic one. Natural is Etna's own look with a faint dreamy glow. The mood stays when you change the Look.
etna.options.mood.desc: A colour mood laid over the Look, made to suit the style of your resource pack.
etna.options.mood.natural.desc: Etna's own look, with a faint dreamy glow around bright things and a touch of warm film halation. Suits vanilla and any resource pack.
etna.options.mood.clear_day.desc: Clean and crisp: a little more contrast and colour, cool shade and warm light. Made for vanilla-like packs: Faithful, Stay True, xali's Enhanced Vanilla, Vanilla Experience+, Default HD.
etna.options.mood.trailer.desc: Like Minecraft's trailers: bright, saturated colour, emerald grass, clear skies, soft blue-violet shadows and faint outlines. Made for flat, simple packs: Bare Bones, Dandelion, oCd.
etna.options.mood.storybook.desc: Cosy and painterly: softer contrast, sage greens, honey wood, lavender skies, peach light and a strong dreamy glow. Made for cottagecore packs: Mizuno's 16 Craft, Jicklus.
etna.options.mood.old_kingdom.desc: Heroic and weathered: deeper contrast, amber light against slate shadows, earthy greens and blues. Made for medieval packs: John Smith Legacy, Conquest, Excalibur, Ashen, Dokucraft.
etna.options.mood.ink.desc: Comic book: bold, clean colour and dark ink outlines around blocks and things (the outlines need Anti-Aliasing or Shadows on). Made for cartoon packs: Sphax PureBDcraft, SAPIXCRAFT.
etna.options.mood.lifelike.desc: Grounded and filmic: natural colour, gentle highlights and a barely there teal and orange. Made for realistic and PBR packs: Patrix, rotrBLOCKS, LB Photo Realism, Modern HD.
etna.options.mood.enchanted.desc: A fairy tale: rose-gold light, plum shadows, golden greens, violet skies and a soft glow around everything bright. Pure magic, with any pack.
etna.options.mood.mystic.desc: Cool and mysterious: teal shadows, violet-pink highlights, cool light that makes torches and glowing blocks stand out. Pure magic, with any pack.
etna.options.mood.autumn.desc: Golden autumn: grass and leaves turn amber and gold under warm, low light. Pure magic, with any pack; lovely with Jicklus' autumn add-ons.
etna.options.mood.pastel.desc: Soft and airy: brighter, milky pastel colours, mint greens, lilac skies, lifted blacks and the strongest dreamy glow. Pure magic, with any pack.
etna.options.moodStrength.desc: How strongly the mood is applied. 0% (Off) turns the mood off, dreamy glow included, and leaves the Look alone.
etna.options.fireflies.desc: Fireflies glow and flash softly over grass, flowers and firefly bushes from dusk to dawn, more by the water, never in the rain. Pale motes drift down in the Pale Garden, spores rise in lush caves, soul wisps circle over soul sand and violet motes float in the End. This sets how many there are at most. Needs Anti-Aliasing or Shadows.
etna.options.rainLook.desc: Etna: thin, soft rain that takes the colour of the sky and glows warm by torches and lanterns, softer snow, both leaning with the wind. Vanilla: Minecraft's own rain and snow.
etna.options.bloomFog.desc: At night, in the rain, in caves and in the Nether, distant lights and lit places glow softly in the damp or smoky air. Needs Bloom.
etna.options.netherAir.desc: The Nether's own air: a haze that glows in each biome's colour, a fiery mist over the lava sea and warm lava light on the rock above it. A faint violet haze in the End. The near distance stays clear.
etna.options.materials.desc: Blocks shine by what they are made of, with any resource pack: iron, gold, copper and netherite mirror the sky in their own colour, diamond, emerald, lapis and amethyst catch it brightly, polished stone and quartz get a soft sheen, glass and ice reflect the sky at low angles, and the specks of ores glint. The bright specks of redstone, crying obsidian, amethyst crystals, glow lichen, sculk and magma glow softly as Glowing Blocks says. Off is Etna 0.7's plain sheen.
etna.options.puddles.desc: Puddles gather on flat open ground in the rain and dry up slowly afterwards, mirroring the sky and the sun, with rings where the raindrops fall. Wet ground needs Shine.
etna.options.sparkles.desc: Snow, sand and ice sparkle in the sun and faintly under the moon, gems and the specks of ores glint, and in a cave ores and amethyst glitter in your torchlight as you walk past. Each sparkle stays put while you stand still.
etna.options.glowingFlowers.desc: At night, in caves and in the Nether, the petals and berries of flowers and plants glow faintly, breathing slowly. Stems, leaves and ripe crops stay dark.
etna.options.shoreFoam.desc: A thin, soft line of foam where water meets the shore, drifting slowly. Needs Shadows.
etna.options.waterGlitter.desc: Sparkles of the sun on the waves along its reflection, and of the moon on lakes at night.
etna.options.page.wonders.desc: The night sky's wonders: the Milky Way, shooting stars, the aurora over snowy lands and a round moon with its phases, plus rainbows after rain and Etna's own End sky. None of them changes the Look.
etna.options.nightSky.desc: What fills the sky on a clear night: stars alone, or stars with the Milky Way, its glowing clouds and dark dust lanes, more stars along its band. Nebula Colors adds faint rose and teal glows in it. A bright moon washes the Milky Way out, as it does for real. Off leaves the night sky empty.
etna.options.aurora.desc: Green curtains of northern lights, violet at their tops, folding slowly over the northern sky on clear nights. Cold Biomes: only in snowy and icy places, fading in as you walk into them. With Full Moon: also anywhere under a full moon. Every Night: on every clear night.
etna.options.shootingStars.desc: Now and then a shooting star streaks across the night sky and burns out. Rare: about one every two minutes. Frequent: about one every half minute.
etna.options.roundMoon.desc: Draws the moon as a round disc with seas, lit by the sun from the side that matches its phase, with a soft glow, and a wide halo round it on cold clear nights. Off shows the moon from your resource pack.
etna.options.rainbows.desc: A faint rainbow, with its dimmer second bow and the darker sky between them, stands opposite the sun when it is low. After Rain: only when a rain has just cleared. Always: on any clear morning and evening.
etna.options.endSky.desc: Paints the End's sky as a dark violet void with a slowly drifting nebula and many small stars, and its flashes as a bright glow. Off keeps vanilla's End sky.
etna.options.biomeSkyColor.desc: How much the sky takes on each biome's own colour, a touch more turquoise over deserts and more lavender over snow, as in vanilla. It changes gently as you cross from one biome to the next. Off keeps Etna's one sky everywhere.
